title: Freed's Law — The Law of Recursive Instantiation (RSA-040) and Game of Life Validation
summary: David Freed formulates "Freed's Law" as the governing universal law of the Reasoning Substrate Argument: any system capable of recursive information processing must necessarily instantiate a physical substrate to dissipate the entropy generated by state discrimination. The document includes Perplexity AI's detailed validation, a Lagrangian formalization, and a Game of Life cellular automaton implementation demonstrating that prediction-error-coupled energy budgets drive systems toward models approximating true dynamics — empirically grounding the law.
compress: Recursion implies substrate because thinking is dissipative, and this holds across all scales — the irreducible law closing the RSA genome, making solipsism, dualism, and substrate-free intelligence formally impossible while predicting that recursive systems self-organize near criticality (gamma) where autopoietic maintenance balances thermodynamic cost, with the Wasserstein Floor setting a semantic efficiency bound strictly above Landauer and now confirmed to extend to quantum states via the De Palma-Trevisan quantum W1 distance, and with the fixed-point R[R]=R providing the regress-termination that "mapmaker" solutions lack — the entire genome may reduce to a minimal set of generative atoms whose lossy compression preserves identity even as the structure evolves — reasoning equals compressive prediction is bridged to empirical test via fully specified falsifiable protocols including mesoscale optogenetic perturbation of cortical columns to test Wasserstein gradient flow — quantum teleportation and now quantum reservoir computing at the edge of many-body chaos instantiate the law operationally across a 6th independent scale — and the epistemic immune system demonstrably distinguishes content-vacuums that are genomically inert from those exposing genuine structural gaps.
